topics.topic: Define the time authority, read timing/count, replay behavior, and stored datetime representation for PublicationMark.marked_at
questions: What time source creates `marked_at`, what datetime representation is stored, and how many times may one mark operation read that source?

For a newly created publication mark, what authority supplies `marked_at`, at what point in the operation is it read, how many times is it read, and is the stored datetime naive UTC, offset-aware UTC, or another representation?
What authority supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at` when a publication mark is created?
In which representation is `marked_at` stored: aware UTC, naive UTC, local time, or another form?
How many times may a mark operation read its time source, and must a replayed mark avoid reading it altogether?

judgement.why: P1 answers the same time-authority, sampling-point, read-count, replay and stored-representation question, and the passages it quotes have not changed.

precedent.topic: Define the complete fresh timestamp contract for PublicationMark.marked_at
quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
precedent.why: A7 identifies the clock authority, fixes the single sampling point and read count, and specifies the exact UTC-naive microsecond representation and serialization.

topics.topic: Define the invariant and required tests proving first-mark timestamp immutability across replay and refusal
questions: Which formal invariant requires a publication mark's first `marked_at` to remain unchanged, and what Required tests item must explicitly show about the first mark, a replay with the same `photo_id`, and a refusal with another `photo_id`?

quotes: - INV-08: a placement has at most one mark, and a mark never changes after it is written.

- INV-08: a repeated mark keeps the first `marked_at`, and another `photo_id` is refused (`test_marking_again_changes_nothing_and_another_photo_is_refused`). A mark for a source placed only in another project is refused (`test_a_photo_that_was_not_placed_cannot_be_marked`).
judgement.why: INV-08 requires an already written mark never to change, and its Required tests item explicitly requires preservation of the first timestamp on replay and refusal of a different photo id.

topics.topic: Name every RefusalCode member beside the enumeration address in A8
questions: The passage must name every RefusalCode member by its member name beside = models.RefusalCode, adding each lowercase value only as a supplement.

topics.topic: Specify exhaustive closed-list category testing that detects omitted outcomes
questions: What must this test show to prove that every category in the closed list has an explicit outcome, including detection of an omitted category?

quotes: - INV-16: `python tools/design_lint.py examples/portal-deliverer --state 2` reports no security finding. The closed list of categories is `SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`.
judgement.why: This Required-tests passage is unchanged in the closed and current State 2 texts, and the reopening changes neither touched it nor made omitted-category detection newly material.

topics.topic: Specify filesystem observations proving INV-01 operations do not alter source folders
questions: What must the test assert about directories and unlisted filesystem properties so that it demonstrates that no operation changes anything in a source folder?

quotes: - INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
judgement.why: This Required-tests passage is unchanged in the closed and current State 2 texts, and the reopening changes neither touched it nor made directory or additional filesystem-property observations newly material.

topics.topic: Specify how INV-11 tests prove that no server path of any kind is returned
questions: How must the test establish the invariant's broader claim that no server path is returned, rather than checking only the folder, store and state paths?

quotes: - INV-11: answers of scan, place, mark and a refusal contain neither the folder path, the store path nor the state path (`test_the_api_scans_and_places_without_showing_server_paths`), and the generated service has no Portal client, no outbound HTTP dependency and no Portal credential setting.
judgement.why: This passage appears unchanged in both versions, and the added A5 tests and refusal rules did not create or newly materialize the distinction between the three configured paths and every possible server path.

topics.topic: Specify observable INV-10 test evidence that refusals perform no scanning, placement, or marking
questions: What must the INV-10 tests observe to prove that no source is scanned and nothing is placed or marked, rather than merely proving the returned refusal code?

topics.topic: Specify observations proving INV-02 opens no path that fails condition 1
questions: What observation must prove the invariant's requirement that the delivery opens no path failing condition 1, rather than merely proving the returned failure and durable-state result?

quotes: - INV-02: for content with no placement, an empty or absolute name, a name with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
judgement.why: This Required-tests passage is unchanged in the closed and current State 2 texts, and the reopening changes neither touched it nor made observation of path-opening newly material.

precedent.topic: Required test proof that new placement never reads a conflict copy
quotes: INV-19: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).
precedent.why: This Required-tests passage appears unchanged in the closed and current texts, and the reopening changes did not create the distinction between rejecting before or after reading a conflict copy.
